body.statement: For every observed law in \(\mathcal M_\eta\), the sharp identified set for \(\mu_{11}\) under Tan's product sensitivity model is exactly \([F_-(P),F_+(P)]\). Both endpoints have the compact formulas in \(\mathrm{def{:}compact\text{-}sharp\text{-}endpoints}\), each is evaluable by at most \(64\) rational branches with the weak branch inequalities in \(\mathcal B_-(P)\) and \(\mathcal B_+(P)\), every active tie gives the same endpoint value, and each endpoint is attained by a full-data law compatible with the complete observed law \(P\).
body.justification: It replaces an implicit coupled sharp program by a closed-form, fully attainable binary frontier.
body.gap: Tan (2025), Lemma 8, gives the exact compatible-law optimization but states that ratio coupling obstructs a general exact unconstrained representation; no finite binary formula is given.
body.consumer: Dickerman et al.'s six-year cancer analysis can report a sharp interval for the absolute risk under a sustained metformin strategy after binary coarsening.
body.proof_tex:
Define the identified set without conflating it with an observed-law functional:
\[
 \Theta_I(P)=\left\{\mathbb E_Q[Y^{1,1}]:
 Q\text{ has observed marginal }P,\ Q\text{ obeys the two consistency assumptions, and its ratios lie in }\mathcal R(P;G,B,C)\right\}.
\]
The cited compatibility-program lemma identifies this set as the image of the reduced feasible set from \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}probability\text{-}reduction}\) under
\[
 M(s,t,h)=a\sum_{\ell=0}^1q_\ell r_\ell
 +(1-a)\{h t_0+(1-h)t_1\},\qquad
 r_\ell=e_\ell p_\ell+(1-e_\ell)s_\ell.
\]
This invocation uses Tan's compatibility result only to relate the causal full-data laws to the observed-law program; the optimization below is derived directly.

The reduced feasible set is nonempty because \(s_\ell=p_\ell\), \(r_\ell=p_\ell\), \(t_\ell=p_\ell\), and \(h=q_0\) are feasible.  It is compact.  It is also convex: besides interval constraints on \(s_\ell\) and \(h\), the restrictions on \((r_\ell,t_\ell)\) are the four linear inequalities
\[
 t_\ell\geq r_\ell/B,\quad t_\ell\geq Br_\ell-(B-1),\quad
 t_\ell\leq Br_\ell,\quad t_\ell\leq 1-(1-r_\ell)/B.
\]
Consequently it is connected, and its continuous real-valued image under \(M\) is a compact interval.

For the upper endpoint, \(0<h<1\) because \(0<q_0<1\) and \(C<\infty\).  Thus, at fixed \((s,h)\), both coefficients of \(t_0,t_1\) in \(M\) are strictly positive, so \(t_\ell=U_B(r_\ell)\).  Both affine pieces defining \(U_B\) have positive slope, hence \(U_B\) is increasing.  The coefficient \(a q_\ell\) of \(r_\ell\) is positive, and therefore the resulting objective is increasing in each \(r_\ell\) and in each \(s_\ell\).  It follows that
\[
 s_\ell=U_G(p_\ell),\quad r_\ell=r_\ell^+,\quad t_\ell=t_\ell^+.
\]
The remaining function of \(h\) is affine, so its maximum over \([h^-,h^+]\) is attained at one of the two endpoints.  This gives exactly \(F_+(P)\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}compact\text{-}sharp\text{-}endpoints}\).  Reversing every monotonicity step gives \(s_\ell=D_G(p_\ell)\), \(r_\ell=r_\ell^-\), \(t_\ell=t_\ell^-\), and the endpoint of \([h^-,h^+]\) minimizing the last affine expression; hence the lower value is exactly \(F_-(P)\).

Compactness gives reduced optimizers.  The compatible ratio lift maps each optimizer into \(\mathcal R(P;G,B,C)\), with positive denominators by the interior assumption.  The cited compatibility-program lemma then supplies a full-data law having the complete observed marginal \(P\) and attaining the corresponding causal mean.  Since the continuous image is an interval, every value between the two attained extrema is also attained.  Therefore
\[
 \Theta_I(P)=[F_-(P),F_+(P)],
\]
so these are sharp bounds, not merely outer bounds.

It remains to verify the finite atlas.  Each of \(U_G(p_0),U_G(p_1),U_B(r_0^+),U_B(r_1^+)\) selects the smaller of two affine pieces; the ordering of \(t_0^+,t_1^+\) selects \(h^-\) or \(h^+\); and the selected covariate envelope selects one of its two affine pieces.  These are six binary choices.  The weak inequalities in \(\mathcal B_+(P)\) are exactly the conditions that the chosen pieces and ordering are active, so substitution gives \(F_+(P)=f_\beta^+(P)\) for an admissible \(\beta\), among at most \(2^6=64\) rational formulas.  The same argument, with maxima of the lower affine pieces and the minimizing ordering, gives \(\mathcal B_-(P)\) and at most \(64\) lower formulas.  At a piece tie the two affine values coincide; at an ordering tie \(t_0^s=t_1^s\), the final affine expression is independent of \(h\).  Thus every simultaneously active tied branch has the same endpoint value.
